title: Batch 2^17 (4x smaller, device batch 64)
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**17 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -> 64 (grad_accum stays 1); eval call pinned to a fixed batch of 128 so val packing is unchanged.
reflection: val_bpb 0.997042 vs baseline 0.997359 — a win, but only -0.0003, far smaller than the batch-size argument predicted. 3184 optimizer steps (roughly 4x baseline) at 417M tokens, steady-state MFU 33.5%, peak VRAM 22.7GB. The read: the batch axis is nearly flat here. Quadrupling the update count bought almost nothing, and the smaller device batch costs real throughput (fewer tokens processed for the same 300s), so the extra steps are being paid for with tokens at close to break-even. Whatever 2^18 measures, I'd expect it in the same 0.9965-0.9975 band rather than a breakthrough, which means the batch knob is a mild tuning gain and not the lever worth more slots. The group should move to axes that change the model's token efficiency itself — depth/width shape (depth 8 at 512 dim is thin), the warmdown fraction, or LRs — rather than spending further runs bracketing batch size.
